decisions.reason: The issue and repair instruction directly identify failed ignition coils; the card names this exact component and does not imply that it repairs a different failure branch.
The prescribed repair directly replaces the PCV/oil-separator assembly named by this exact part proposal.
The updated tensioner is an explicitly prescribed timing-service component and is labeled as a tensioner rather than as a complete kit.
The article distinguishes cracked glass from frame, seal, drain, impact, and alignment causes; the glass link needs the glass-damage branch to be confirmed first.
The repair may be cleaning, EGR-valve replacement, or EGR-cooler replacement; the valve link must be gated to a confirmed valve fault.
The article requires VCDS deviation testing and allows cleaning before replacing only the failed injector; the current proposal has no diagnostic condition.
The CBEA slice still requires VCDS deviation testing and confirmation of the individual failed injector before commerce is shown.

The issue is turbocharger failure and the repair explicitly prescribes this turbocharger component; required oil lines and gaskets remain separate prescribed items rather than changing this part's role.
The primary repair is clearing the drains; hose replacement is prescribed only when a drain connection is cracked, which the proposal cannot yet express.
The issue and repair instruction directly call for rear upper shock-mount replacement, matching this exact component role.
The upper timing-chain tensioner is explicitly prescribed as one accurately labeled component of the complete timing service.
The article lists fluid service, valve-body work, torque-converter replacement, or a rebuild depending on scan, slip, and debris evidence; a blanket converter link is unsafe.
The thermostat is explicitly included in the prescribed cooling-system replacement and the proposal labels it only as that component.
The tensioner is explicitly prescribed and accurately labeled as one component of the complete chain, tensioner, and guide service.
The article separates bearing, bypass-valve, and boost-hose failures; this valve link is valid only after the bypass-valve branch is confirmed.
The water pump is directly prescribed for this water-pump/thermostat failure and is truthfully labeled as the pump rather than a complete repair kit.
Light rust should be cleared by braking and refinishing is another branch; rotor purchase is appropriate only when deep corrosion or warping is confirmed.
The leak may require clearing or rerouting drains, repairing the tray, or replacing a cracked channel; the hose link lacks that branch confirmation.
The issue is compressor failure and the stated repair directly replaces the A/C compressor; access method and labor do not change the component role.
The article does not identify the failed corner and the proposal's generic front-strut label does not establish a side-specific selectable application.
The article requires boost logging and linkage inspection and may require an actuator, an entire turbocharger, or carbon cleaning; actuator commerce needs a confirmed serviceable-actuator branch.
The tensioner is one explicitly prescribed and accurately labeled component of the full rear timing service, not represented as the complete kit.
The prescribed repair directly replaces the thermostat housing assembly identified by the proposal.
The article covers both strut and compressor failures and requires checking air lines; a compressor link needs compressor-failure evidence rather than a generic suspension symptom.
The article prescribes the revised water-pump/thermostat module; a loose thermostat gasket is supporting hardware and is not the stated failed repair component.
This arm is a valid member of the front-arm repair, but the article requires play inspection to identify which arm is worn before selecting the left-rearward upper arm.
This arm is a valid member of the front-arm repair, but the article requires play inspection to identify which arm is worn before selecting the right-rearward upper arm.
The How-to-Fix prescribes worn front control arms; it does not prescribe a standalone left tie-rod end for this control-arm and ball-joint issue.
The How-to-Fix prescribes worn front control arms; it does not prescribe a standalone right tie-rod end for this control-arm and ball-joint issue.
The article requires cylinder localization and distinguishes injectors, plugs, coils, and carbon; this injector link needs a confirmed failed or leaking injector branch.
The article explicitly recommends replacing the spark plugs as a set during the shared-access coil repair, matching the set-of-eight component label.
The repair explicitly requires both engine mounts as a pair, while this proposal supplies only the right mount and no paired left-mount proposal.
The prescribed repair is the complete timing-belt, tensioner, roller, and water-pump service; a loose water-pump gasket is supporting hardware rather than the identified repair component.
The left-forward lower arm is a valid repair component only after inspection identifies play or torn rubber at that specific arm.
The left-rearward lower arm is a valid repair component only after inspection identifies play or torn rubber at that specific arm.
The right-rearward lower arm is a valid repair component only after inspection identifies play or torn rubber at that specific arm.
The TSB procedure must distinguish a leaking HPFP from leaking injectors; this pump link cannot be shown as the repair before the pressure-decay branch is confirmed.
The issue may be an air spring, compressor, valve block, height sensor, or leak; compressor commerce requires a confirmed compressor failure after leak isolation.
The article requires inspecting bushings, ball joints, and tie rods and does not identify the left side; this complete left-arm link needs a side-specific failed-arm diagnosis.
